research.label: Dogs Trust: enrichment ideas for bored dogs

substitutes: No lick mat? Use a spoon of plain food spread on a clean plate, or skip food.
variations: Home version: wander the yard or hallway, treat on the balcony or a mat, rest by a window.
No food: swap the treat stop for a favorite toy and a gentle fuss.
Slow Sunday version: shorten the wander and double the rest.
Short version: three stops within a single park, twenty minutes in all.
title: The Three-Stop Doggy Date
clue: Three stops, three moods, and the evening ends quieter than it began.
reveal: A date built like a little itinerary: a lively wander, a treat stop, then a proper rest on a blanket that smells of home. Each stop is calmer than the last, so you both finish the outing relaxed rather than rushed.
objective: Take a short three-stop outing that runs from lively to peaceful, with a treat stop in the middle and a real rest at the end.
instructions: Plan three stops within an easy walk, each calmer than the one before: a Wander (park, quiet lane or green corner), a Treat stop (a bench or lawn) and a Rest (a shady bench or quiet corner).
Check every stop in advance: leash rules, hours and any fees. Stick to outdoor public spaces; no shops or cafes needed.

Pack the leash, water and bowl, waste bags, a small mat and a familiar blanket from home (the Rest stop surprise). Bring a treat item such as a lick mat or a portion of your dog's regular food, and your own snack.
Stop 1, Wander: walk at an easy pace and let your dog sniff as much as they like. This is the liveliest part, so enjoy it, then head on when your dog begins to slow.
Stop 2, Treat: lay the mat, offer water first, then give the treat item while you enjoy yours. If your dog is unsettled, skip the food and just sit together.

Stop 3, Rest: spread the blanket from home on the grass or bench seat and let your dog discover it. Put the phone away and sit for ten quiet minutes while they settle on the smell of home, watch the world or doze. Nothing is asked of them.
Head home by the shortest easy route, and offer water when you arrive.
twist: The date follows an energy arc, each stop calmer than the last, and ends with a Rest stop where your dog finds a blanket from home waiting.
completion: Counts once you have visited all three stops, or the first two plus a rest wherever your dog is happiest.
photoIdea: Your dog settled on the blanket from home at the Rest stop, watching the view, taken from slightly behind without any prompting.
memoryPrompt: Which stop did your dog enjoy most, and how did they greet the blanket from home?
supplies: A lick mat or a small portion of regular food

reservation.note: Use outdoor public spaces only. Check leash rules and closing times before you go.

dietNotes: Use a small portion of your dog's regular food, counted in the day's meals. Ask your vet about diet. Food-free option included.
safety: Check leash rules and opening hours; stay in outdoor public spaces and never leave your dog tied up or alone.
Check the ground with your hand; skip hot pavement and offer water at every stop.
Choose quiet times; leave if your dog is uneasy, panting hard or wants to go home.
